newsitem.title: FRANCE: Publicis's True North stake fixed till end-1998.
newsitem.headline: Publicis's True North stake fixed till end-1998.

text.p: French advertising agency Publicis will hold its 20 percent stake in True North until December 31, 1998, under a standstill agreement between the two groups, Publicis chairman Maurice Levy said.
"After that we will see what we do," he told a news conference.

Publicis earlier said it settled a year-long dispute with its former U.S. ally True North, the Chicago-based parent of Foote, Cone & Belding, the largest U.S. advertising agency. Publicis will now develop a global network of agenices under its own name and transfer to True North the FCB agenices in Paris, London, Lisbon and Athen.

"We have not totally untied our links because of a problem of valuing Publicis Communication. We did not want to buy True North's stake in Publicis Communication ourselves and we are the only possible buyers, for the price they asked," Levy said.

Following the accord Publicis Communication, the group's advertising operating unit, will be owned 73.5 percent by Publicis SA and 26.5 percent by True North, against 79.2 percent for Publicis and 20.8 percent for True North previously.
